@graph.headline: Keep, Consolidate, or Replace: Auditing the Stack You Already Own
@graph.description: Most technology audits count licenses and cancel the unused ones. The stack that decides whether a business compounds is three layers — website, private AI, verified workflows — and each one has a different keep-or-replace test. Here are the tests, the real cost of replacement, and a 90-minute audit you can run yourself.

about.name: Business technology stack audit — a three-layer review of an existing Metro Detroit business stack (professional website, local LLM device for private AI, Chainlink Runtime Environment verified workflows) measured against three tests: asset custody (what the business still holds if the vendor disappears), evidence (what the layer can prove about itself with baselines, logs, or exports), and survivability (whether it survives a change of vendor, model, or platform). Includes migration recovery data for website replacement (median 304 days across 1,052 migrations, 64% of platform switches losing page-one rankings), SaaS waste benchmarks (118 apps per company, 36% of licenses unused), guidance on keeping local LLM hardware while re-evaluating model weights against a pre-launch evaluation set, the export test for verifiable workflow records, and a 90-minute self-service audit.

mainEntity.name: What is a technology stack audit?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is a review of the layers a business runs on — website, private AI, verified workflows — measured on asset custody, evidence, and survivability. It differs from a software spend audit, which counts licenses and produces savings, not capability.

mainEntity.name: Should I rebuild my website or keep it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Keep it if you own the domain, content, and analytics account and the site can hold separate pages for services, locations, and proof without a developer. Rebuild if it is a single landing page that cannot hold page structure. Rebuilding a site that already ranks carries a median 304-day recovery.

mainEntity.name: How much traffic do you lose migrating a website?

acceptedAnswer.text: A clean, well-mapped migration typically loses 10–30% of organic traffic in the first month. Median full recovery runs about 304 days across 1,052 migrations, and roughly 14% never fully recover. Sloppy moves with redirect gaps lose 30–50% or more.

mainEntity.name: Do I have to replace my local LLM hardware when a new model arrives?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Hardware, model weights, retrieval corpus, and evaluation set are separable. Keep the device, swap the weights, and re-run your evaluation set to confirm the new model is better on your work rather than on a benchmark.

mainEntity.name: How do I know whether a workflow's records will survive a vendor change?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask for an export before you sign and again after thirty days. If you can produce a record of which steps ran, when, and against which data without the vendor's dashboard, the record is yours. If you cannot, you are renting it.
